value: In free fall the acceleration stays constant (g) throughout
reasoning: A freely falling body moves under gravity alone, so its acceleration is g at every instant. A ball thrown up has zero velocity at the top yet still accelerates at g, so C is false, and a body moving at constant velocity has zero acceleration, so A is false.
The tangent to a field line gives the field direction at a point. If two lines crossed, the field would have two directions at one point, which is impossible, so field lines never intersect.

value: Fleming's left hand rule gives the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
reasoning: The left hand rule (motor rule) gives the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field. The right hand rule (generator rule) gives the direction of the induced current, so B and C are wrong.

value: Every simple harmonic motion is periodic, but not every periodic motion is SHM
reasoning: SHM repeats itself after a fixed time period, so it is always periodic. The converse fails: the Earth's orbit or a bouncing ball is periodic without being simple harmonic.
A speed radar sends out waves and measures the change in frequency of the waves reflected from a moving vehicle. That frequency shift with relative motion is the Doppler effect.

value: The claim that the third law implies a cause-effect relation is NOT correct
reasoning: Action and reaction act simultaneously, so neither is the cause of the other; the third law implies no cause-effect relation (D is correct). Forces always occur in pairs (A) and a stone pulls the Earth up as the Earth pulls it down (B), so C is the incorrect statement.

value: Magnesium is used in fireworks to make a bright white light
reasoning: Magnesium burns with a dazzling white flame, which is why it is used in fireworks, flares and flash powder. Barium compounds are used for X-ray of the alimentary canal, and chlorine for purifying water.

value: Thiourea (accelerator) is not an ingredient of paint
reasoning: Paint consists of a pigment (such as titanium dioxide), a vehicle or drying oil, a thinner (such as turpentine), driers, extenders and anti-skinning agents (such as polyhydroxy phenols). An accelerator like thiourea belongs to rubber vulcanisation, not paint.

value: Ruby's red colour is NOT due to beryllium (it is due to chromium)
reasoning: Ruby is aluminium oxide whose red colour comes from traces of chromium; beryllium is found in emerald and beryl. Strontium gives a crimson flame and magnesium is part of chlorophyll, so those are true. Runner-up B: strictly it is barium sulphate, not barium metal, that is used in the barium meal, so B could also be read as untrue, but D is the clear factual error intended.
Neon glows a bright reddish orange when an electric discharge passes through it, which is the colour of classic neon signs. Helium gives a pinkish glow and argon a lavender or blue one.

Permanent hardness comes from chlorides and sulphates of calcium and magnesium, which boiling cannot remove. An ion-exchange resin (or zeolite) swaps these Ca and Mg ions for sodium or hydrogen ions. Boiling and lime treatment (Clark's method) remove only temporary hardness.

value: Polyaromatic hydrocarbons are not a component of photochemical smog
reasoning: Photochemical smog forms when sunlight acts on nitrogen oxides and hydrocarbons, producing ozone, nitric oxide, peroxyacetyl nitrate (PAN), acrolein and formaldehyde. Polyaromatic hydrocarbons are soot-type pollutants, not a listed component of this smog.
Eukaryotic chromatin is DNA wound around histone proteins to form nucleosomes, together with non-histone proteins. Its essential components are DNA and protein.
Flatworms (Platyhelminthes) are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic and acoelomate. Porifera and Cnidaria are not triploblastic and bilateral, while Annelida have a true coelom.
Gas exchange happens across the thin walls of the alveoli, which are surrounded by blood capillaries. The nasal passage, trachea and bronchi only conduct air.

Adrenaline, secreted into the blood by the adrenal glands, speeds up the heartbeat to prepare the body for emergencies. Thyroxine controls metabolism, insulin blood sugar and testosterone male characteristics.

value: The chemicals (neurotransmitters) are released from the nerve endings
reasoning: The impulse travels along the axon to its end, where the nerve endings release chemicals that cross the synapse to the next neuron. Runner-up D (axon): the endings are the tips of the axon, but the release happens at the terminal endings, not along the axon itself.
Platelets gather at a wound and release factors that start blood clotting. Oxygen transport is the work of red cells, and immunity and phagocytosis belong to white cells.
The de Broglie wavelength is h/p, so equal wavelengths mean equal momentum p. Their energies differ because the photon's energy is pc while the electron's is p squared over 2m.

Water molecules attract each other far more strongly than they attract the non-polar oil molecules, so the two keep separate with an interface held by interfacial (surface) tension. Bulk modulus, shear strain and 'volume effect' have nothing to do with mixing.

value: Solid, liquid and vapour phases all co-exist
reasoning: The triple point is the unique temperature and pressure at which the solid, liquid and vapour phases of a substance exist together in equilibrium.

value: Latent heat is absorbed or released at constant temperature
reasoning: During a change of state, heat is taken in or given out without any change in temperature; that is what latent heat means. Runner-up C (pressure): the change also happens at constant pressure, but the defining feature is constant temperature, and volume does change, so D is wrong.

value: The statement that kinetic energy does not change with frequency is NOT correct
reasoning: By Einstein's equation, the maximum kinetic energy equals hv minus the work function, so it rises as frequency rises above the threshold. Einstein's 1921 Nobel was for this explanation, a threshold frequency exists, and the number of electrons is proportional to intensity, so A, B and D are true.
Chlorine is about 75% Cl-35 and 25% Cl-37, so its average atomic mass is 0.75 x 35 + 0.25 x 37 = 35.5 u.
Tropolone is a seven-membered ring made only of carbon atoms (a carbocyclic, non-benzenoid aromatic). Furan (O), thiophene (S) and pyridine (N) each have a hetero atom in the aromatic ring.
Bauxite is hydrated aluminium oxide (the ore of aluminium), not a silicate. Feldspar, zeolite and mica are all naturally occurring aluminosilicates.
Glycolysis, which breaks glucose into two molecules of pyruvate, takes place in the cytoplasm. Pyruvate is then taken into the mitochondria for aerobic respiration.

value: Ovule becomes the seed and ovary becomes the fruit
reasoning: After fertilisation the ovule develops into the seed and the ovary ripens into the fruit.

value: Glucose breaks down to CO2, H2O and energy in aerobic tissues
reasoning: Complete aerobic respiration gives carbon dioxide, water and energy. It does not happen in all organisms (anaerobes differ, so A is wrong); muscle cells short of oxygen make lactic acid, not ethanol (B wrong); and yeast makes ethanol, not lactate (D wrong).
Intercropping is growing two or more crops at the same time on the same field in a definite row pattern. Crop rotation is growing different crops one after another in different seasons.
Sania Mirza won the Fed Cup Heart Award in May 2020 (Asia/Oceania zone), the first Indian to receive it. Sindhu and Saina are badminton players and Hima Das an athlete.
National Technology Day is observed on 11 May to mark the Pokhran-II nuclear tests of 11 May 1998.
Under Mission Sagar, INS Kesari sailed on 10 May 2020 carrying food and COVID-related medical supplies to Maldives, Mauritius, Seychelles, Madagascar and Comoros.

In the 2019-20 Budget Estimates corporation tax was the largest item, about 7.66 lakh crore rupees (around 21 paise of each rupee), ahead of GST at about 6.6 lakh crore (around 19 paise). Runner-up A (GST): it was close behind, and would win only if a later revised figure were used.
MSME stands for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, the category defined under the MSMED Act, 2006.

Sweden topped the World Economic Forum's Energy Transition Index 2020 (its third year at the top), followed by Switzerland. The '74th' in the stem appears to come from India's rank (74th) in that edition.
Operation Sadbhavna is the Indian Army's welfare and goodwill programme in Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, running schools, health care and infrastructure projects.
A Wing Commander in the Air Force is equivalent to a Lieutenant Colonel in the Army and a Commander in the Navy.
The MNRE 'Development of Solar Cities' programme aims at a minimum 10% reduction in the projected demand for conventional energy at the end of five years, through renewables and energy efficiency.
The name Amphan (meaning sky) was contributed by Thailand to the 2004 list of north Indian Ocean cyclone names; it was the last name on that list.
Natural change of population is the difference between births and deaths, so it is the birth rate minus the death rate (migration is left out).

A spit is a narrow ridge of sand or shingle attached to the land at one end with the other end in open water. A bar has no attachment at either end (or closes a bay), and a tombolo joins an island to the mainland.

value: Protecting communities from earthquakes is not a role of coral reefs
reasoning: Coral reefs support fisheries and tourism jobs, supply limestone building material and break waves to protect coasts from storms. They cannot protect anyone from earthquakes, which are tectonic.

value: All three statements about the Acacia are correct
reasoning: School geography describes the savanna Acacia as having long, wide-spreading roots to find moisture, thorny leaves to cut water loss and a wide umbrella-shaped crown that spreads its foliage to the sun. Runner-up B (2 and 3 only): it wins if the examiner treats Acacia roots as deep tap roots, making 'long shallow root system' wrong.
Dardic languages such as Kashmiri and Shina belong to the Indo-Aryan branch of the Indo-European family.

value: Domestic workers is not one of the four Census categories
reasoning: Census 2011 classified workers as cultivators, agricultural labourers, household industry workers and other workers. 'Domestic workers' is not a separate category.

PLFS 2017-18 put about 11.7% of urban male workers in construction (nearly one-tenth) and about 25% of urban female workers in manufacturing (nearly one-fourth). About 73% of rural female workers were in agriculture, nearly three-fourths, so statement 3 is wrong. Runner-up A (2 only): it would win only if 11.7% were not accepted as nearly one-tenth.
Quantity falls from 30 to 20, a change of 10/30 = 33.3%; price rises from 12 to 15, a change of 3/12 = 25%. Elasticity = 33.3 / 25 = 1.33.
Food inflation tracks food articles and manufactured food items such as cereals and sugar. Tobacco is not a food item and is counted separately (under non-food or pan, tobacco and intoxicants).

value: Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Punjab
reasoning: The NCERT account says that in the first phase (mid-1960s to mid-1970s) HYV seeds were restricted to the more affluent states such as Punjab, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu. Runner-up D (Punjab and Haryana only): Haryana was also an early Green Revolution state, so a key built on that would pick D or B.

value: The steatite seal is the most distinctive Harappan artefact
reasoning: NCERT describes the Harappan seal, made of steatite, as possibly the most distinctive artefact of the civilisation. Runner-up B (1 and 2): bricks of a standardised ratio are also a hallmark of Harappan building, and B wins if the examiner counts them as an artefact. Gold bangles and a silver spittoon are not distinctive Harappan markers.
The Buddhist list of sixteen mahajanapadas includes Kuru, Vatsa and Gandhara but not Kalinga, which became prominent later and was conquered by Ashoka.

value: Both studying the Vedas and engaging in trade
reasoning: The Dharmashastras assigned the Vaishyas the study of the Vedas, performing sacrifices and making gifts, like the Kshatriyas, and in addition agriculture, pastoralism and trade.

The Satavahanas ruled the Deccan and parts of western India. The Sudarshana lake was repaired by the Shaka ruler Rudradaman (Junagadh inscription), and earlier by Skandagupta's governor, not by the Satavahanas.

value: The claim that fundamental duties cannot be used to judge constitutionality is NOT correct
reasoning: The Supreme Court has held that courts may look to a fundamental duty when deciding whether a law is reasonable and constitutional. The duties were added in 1976 (A true), include safeguarding public property and abjuring violence (B true) and are not enforceable by writs (C true).

A Governor has constitutional discretion where the Constitution expressly allows it, and acts independently of the state ministry when appointed administrator of an adjoining Union Territory. Merely disagreeing with the Council of Ministers gives no discretion, so statement 1 is wrong.

value: Socialists do NOT see class divisions as irremediable
reasoning: Socialists see class divisions, based on unequal income and wealth, as a product of the economic system that can and should be removed. They stress community and distribution according to need, so A, B and D are true of socialism.

Pluralist democracy relies on groups to keep government responsive (4); people's democracy seeks social equality through common ownership (3); developmental democracy aims at the fullest development of individual capacities (2); elitist theory holds that power is always held by a privileged few (1).
Airports Authority of India is a Miniratna (Category I) CPSU. Indian Oil and SAIL are Maharatnas and HAL is a Navratna.
Since 2010 the HDI education index uses mean years of schooling (adults 25 and over) and expected years of schooling. Adult literacy and gross enrolment ratio were used before 2010.
Adam Smith's 'invisible hand' is the self-regulating market, where prices guide individuals pursuing their own interest to serve society's needs.

CACP recommends Minimum Support Prices for wheat and rice, a price floor at which the government stands ready to buy so farmers are protected. Runner-up A (Administered Price): MSP is a form of government-fixed price, and a key that treats all government-set prices as administered prices would pick A.
India's mobile telecom market is dominated by a few large operators (Jio, Airtel, Vodafone Idea, BSNL) whose decisions affect each other, which is an oligopoly.
